sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fast-Casual Self-Serve Broth Bowl Master Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid mixed legal system: Roman-Dutch common law, English law procedural influence, constitutional supremacy, and unitary national company-law regime under the Companies Act 71 of 2008
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreement and Protocol between South Africa and the People's Republic of China (signed 25 April 2000; effective 2001)
SACU Agreement, 2002 and SACU trade and investment facilitation framework
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment, 2006 (investment protection principles)
Protection of Investment Act 22 of 2015 (domestic investment protection regime applicable to South African incorporated entities)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), sections 1, 20A, 21, 21A, 21C, 22, 28, 28A and 29, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 and the General Laws Amendment Act 22 of 2022, including the beneficial-owner definition in section 1, the beneficial-ownership register requirements and CIPC Form CoR 44; Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R603 of 28 April 2011), as amended; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act 12 of 2004; FIC Guidance Notes on beneficial ownership, PEPs, sanctions and CDD. For the CIPC register, a 5% direct or indirect interest or effective control may trigger disclosure; for the bank/AML safe-harbour review in this low-risk engagement, the 25% threshold is adopted as the primary screening line, supplemented by control-based tests.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of national identity document or passport of each proposed shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Commissioner of Oaths in the country of document origin; for Mainland China, local notary office followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication step
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the originating state is an Apostille Convention party; for Mainland China, notarization then apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorised provincial foreign affairs office; for non-Apostille states, South African consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of good standing and constitutional documents of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or its local Market Supervision Administration office for a PRC corporate shareholder; equivalent company registry for other jurisdictions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Official registry extract notarized and apostilled by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorised provincial foreign affairs office; for non-Apostille states, South African consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholder resolution approving the incorporation of the South African (Pty) Ltd and appointing authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's board of directors, recorded by its company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, where required by CIPC, the participating bank or the South African revenue/corporate authority, Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed by proposed shareholders and directors in favor of the South African incorporation agent or attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable; executed original retained in the AML/KYC file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds/wealth statement for each 25% or greater ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed ultimate beneficial owner, witnessed by a notary public or Commissioner of Oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized declaration; apostille required only when the declaration is to be used cross-border as a public document before CIPC, banks or other accountable institutions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential or business address for each director, shareholder and beneficial owner (utility bill or regulated bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized/certified copy; if issued by a public authority and challenged by the bank or regulator, Hague Apostille or consular legalization may be required depending on the issuing state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening is required for all proposed directors, shareholders, 25% or greater UBOs, the proposed franchise principal, and the authorized incorporation agent. Screening must be run against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions database, the South African domestic targeted financial sanctions list, and any FIC/DTIC terrorist asset-freezing notices. PEP status is assessed under the FIC Act definitions; adverse results require enhanced due diligence, senior-management sign-off, and, if unresolved, a suspicious transaction report under sections 28A and 29 of FICA. Ongoing screening is to be repeated at each subsequent KYC refresh and before each royalty-wire payment milestone.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services online transaction portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) at https://www.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered company names must be represented in the Latin alphabet. South African official languages are accepted, but Chinese characters or non-Latin script may not be entered in the CIPC registered-name field. For the proposed Chinese Malatang self-serve brand, the registered name must be an English or romanized transliteration such as 'Chinese Malatang Self Serve (Pty) Ltd'; the Chinese script may remain a colloquial trade-name/brand only and cannot form the statutory company name. Names are limited to the prescribed character length and must be distinctive without being misleading as to the nature or scale of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC refuses a name reservation, the applicant receives an electronic refusal notice in CIPC e-Services. The applicant may (i) request written reasons within 15 business days of the refusal, (ii) file a reconsideration request through the CIPC e-Services name-reservations queue with a distinguishing element or proof of prior ministerial consent for a sensitive token, or (iii) submit a fresh name application using a different distinctive formulation. A reservation is valid for six months from grant and may be renewed once before expiry by application to CIPC if the incorporation has not yet been completed. If CIPC confirms the refusal after reconsideration, the aggrieved applicant may institute judicial review in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 and the applicable Companies Act provisions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted virtual-office acceptance. A virtual registered office may be used for the statutory seat and CIPC record-keeping of this non-operating franchise and licensing vehicle, provided physical records are accessible for SARS/CIPC/law-enforcement inspection and the address is not misleading. The underlying fast-casual Malatang restaurant premises cannot be virtual: the operational restaurant, whether company-owned or franchised, requires a physical licensed location under municipal health, food-safety, zoning and business-licensing requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderately low for the holding/licensing entity and moderately higher for the operational food premises: CIPC physical inspection of the registered office is estimated at below 5% in the first 12 months; SARS/auditor premises visits approximately 10-15%; municipal environmental-health and labour inspectorate unannounced site visits at the licensed restaurant are estimated at 30-40% once food-service operations commence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name reservation search, clearance and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under CIPC fee schedule (ZAR 50, converted at approximately USD 3.50)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and registration of the private (Pty) Ltd company with CIPC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under CIPC fee schedule (ZAR 175, converted at approximately USD 11.00)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024, read with Sections 13, 14, 19 and 66; Companies Regulations 2011 prescribed in Form CoR 14.1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or issued capital for a Proprietary Limited company; shareholders may authorise 100 ordinary no-par-value shares; there is no mandatory escrow deposit or bank account verification requirement under the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVED BY THE INITIAL DIRECTORS: 1. The subscription for 100 ordinary no-par-value shares by the founding shareholders is approved and the initial capital has been credited to the company's account. 2. The registered office of the company shall be the address in Johannesburg, South Africa, as entered in the notice of incorporation. 3. The following persons [name / ID number] are appointed as directors, and [name] is appointed as financial officer, each to serve from the date of incorporation. 4. The directors are authorised to submit the notice of incorporation, execute banking instructions, engage SARS, and take all lawful steps to carry the company's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and corporate due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 9.1 for reservation of up to four proposed company names; verify availability against CIPC database and reserve the preferred name for the statutory 60-day period.
required_dossiers: Director full names and identity or passport numbers
Residential address details for servicing agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a name objection query, file an amended name application within 20 business days or submit supporting evidence of consent from mark holders for the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and initial consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC-approved company secretary or corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI in compliance with the Companies Act incorporating the reserved name, authorised share allocation, internal governance rules, registered address, and first director appointments; obtain signed letters of consent from initial directors.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act notices for all initial directors
Identity or passport copies of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any typographical or statutory inconsistencies in the MOI and re-submit the corrected document for certification before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 14.1 electronically via CIPC e-Services together with the signed MOI and name reservation details; pay CIPC filing fees and obtain the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and company registration number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CIPC verification or query notice within 20 business days; provide required certified supporting documents or amend the application to cure any disclosed defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with South African Revenue Service for a newly incorporated company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Income Tax on Form IT77; register for VAT, PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy as applicable; provide banking details and a valid public officer appointment.
required_dossiers: Banking account details of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects or marks registration incomplete, contact the SARS branch via eFiling objections, submit amended information, and obtain a reference number before escalating to the SARS Registration Helpline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration statutory records, share certificates, and board minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the statutory records required under Section 24 of Companies Act, including securities register, directors' register, filing history and minute book; issue share certificates within ten days of subscription; record first board meeting minutes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify incomplete statutory registers and file supplementary resolutions or correction statements with CIPC where an annotation is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Environmental Health Services under the National Health Act 61 of 2003, together with the Department of Labour occupational compliance units
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Acceptability for Food Premises (CoA) under Regulation 962 of 2012 and Business Trading Licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from compulsory full EIA for a standard fast-casual restaurant in an existing commercial zoning; municipal land-use and environmental health authorisation required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Oils and grease in wastewater to municipal sewer must be below 25 mg/l; grease traps must be maintained; local air quality by-law nuisance for cooking fumes and odours must be respected; solid waste handling must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency Services Certificate confirming suppression systems and unobstructed escape routes; Municipal Building Control Certificate of Occupancy under the National Building Regulations; Occupational Health and Safety Act compliance clearance including personal protective equipment, ventilation inspections, electrical certificates, and first aid provision.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; governing statutes: Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, Customs Control Act 31 of 2014, and the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual (Exchange Control Regulations 1961).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and obtain the company registration number; appoint a resident public officer within one month under s 246 Tax Administration Act. 2) Register on the SARS eFiling portal for income tax and obtain the Income Tax reference number within 30 days of incorporation. 3) Register as a VAT vendor (form VAT 101) within 21 days of triggering compulsory registration; voluntarily register once taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000 in 12 months. 4) Register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL (form EMP 101) within 14 days of becoming an employer. 5) Submit the CIPC certificate, memorandum of incorporation, directors' ID/passport copies, and bank proof of address; foreign shareholding is unrestricted. 6) Obtain a Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN for municipal food-services licensing and government procurement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A resident (Pty) Ltd is subject to national income tax at the entity level at 27% (from 2023) on worldwide income, with an 80% capital-gain inclusion rate, 20% dividends withholding tax, and no pass-through regime. A qualifying entity with gross income up to ZAR 20 million may access Small Business Corporation progressive rates (0%/7%/21%). Controlled foreign company passive income may be imputed to the resident shareholder under s 9D.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box election; classification is statutory. Available elections: (i) Small Business Corporation status under s 12E claimed on assessment; (ii) Headquarter Company election under s 9I for companies held at least 80% by non-residents (tax-neutral foreign dividends, interest, royalties and CFC inclusions); (iii) VAT grouping election for associated companies under s 50 VAT Act; (iv) CFC elections under s 9D, including the election to treat a CFC as resident in limited instances; (v) s 23N election allocating the interest-limitation formula in cross-border financing. Hybrid mismatch rules (ss 8F, 8FA, 23N, 25D) are mandatory, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991; invoice-and-credit mechanism with bi-monthly VAT 201 returns (monthly for turnover exceeding ZAR 50 million).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 in the preceding 12 months or reasonably expected in the next 12 months (s 23(1)). Voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 in the preceding 12 months (s 24). Foreign suppliers of electronic services register at a ZAR 50,000 annual threshold (s 23A).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS phased e-invoicing mandate (Draft Rules 2024): voluntary from 1 July 2025; mandatory for VAT vendors with turnover above ZAR 10 million from 1 September 2025; mandatory for all other VAT vendors from 1 September 2026. Invoices must be issued in the SARS-approved structured XML format (UBL 2.1-aligned) and transmitted digitally via the SARS eInvoicing gateway or a certified service provider, with digital signature and unique invoice identifier; there is no pre-issuance fiscal clearance approval, but s 20 VAT Act tax-invoice and s 55 record-keeping rules apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: s 11(1)(a) VAT Act where goods are consigned to a non-resident and physically removed from South Africa within 90 days of supply. Services: s 11(2)(l) where services are supplied to a non-resident recipient and are not directly connected with land or movable property in South Africa; franchise and royalty fees from non-resident master franchisees are zero-rated when the licensor's services are physically performed outside South Africa or the benefit is consumed offshore. The vendor bears the burden of proof and must retain prescribed documentary evidence within the statutory period under s 11(3); input VAT on procurement may be refunded against export supplies on the VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS SAD500 Customs Export Declaration (bill of entry)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical removal from South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate confirming receipt of export or franchise proceeds
Commercial invoice and zero-rated VAT invoice (s 20 VAT Act compliant)
Foreign master-franchise or royalty agreement (for services zero-rating)
Bank statement and SARB exchange-control records
Packing list, consignment note and weight certificate (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits zero-rating retrospectively: failure to obtain export proof or physical removal within 90 days triggers output VAT clawback under s 16(2)(e) VAT Act with interest, plus additional tax under s 60 VAT Act of up to 200% of the tax evaded. The Tax Administration Act s 223 understatement penalties apply at 10% (substantial understatement), 25% (lack of reasonable care), 50% (no reasonable grounds) and 100% (intentional tax evasion), with interest under s 187. Non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days leads to SARB exchange-control enquiries, suspension of tax clearance and potential criminal exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, the Exchange Control Regulations of 1961, and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA). Day-to-day administration is delegated to Category I Authorised Dealers, being the licensed South African commercial banks, which execute all inward and outward foreign-exchange transactions and balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand is freely tradable offshore but remains subject to a regulated exchange-control framework administered by FinSurv and the Authorised Dealers. Current-account transactions, including settlement of genuine trade import invoices, service fees, after-tax dividends to non-resident shareholders, and approved royalty/licence fees, are permitted without individual FinSurv approval provided supporting documentation is presented and the transaction is recorded through an Authorised Dealer for BOP purposes. Capital-account transactions are liberalised for inward foreign direct investment: a non-resident shareholder may subscribe for shares in a South African Pty Ltd without prior SARB approval, but the funds must enter through an Authorised Dealer as an inward transfer, and the foreign shareholder must not be part of a prohibited loop structure. Profit-remittance hurdles are administrative rather than prohibitive: a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN is required for any individual remittance exceeding ZAR 10 million, dividends must be declared in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and paid timeously after finalisation of the annual financial statements, and the original share capital must have been duly recorded on the BOP reporting system. The master franchise entity in scope is primarily a ZAR-generating domestic business with optional inbound USD/CNY capital and outbound royalty/trade flows; no convertibility blockage is present for lawful commercial flows, but non-resident financing routed through opaque conduits will attract enhanced domestic and correspondent-bank scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers (Section B) and the FinSurv directives applicable from 2021, exporters must repatriate foreign-currency export proceeds to South Africa through an Authorised Dealer within 180 days from the date of shipment; extensions to 365 days require Authorised Dealer approval, and longer periods require FinSurv consent. The statutory mandatory conversion or surrender requirement was abolished in January 2021, so the mandatory conversion ratio is nil (0%) and exporters may elect to retain proceeds in approved Foreign Currency Accounts or convert at commercial market rates. Exporters must nevertheless present proof of receipt, usually the SWIFT MT103 credit advice matching the export invoice, the SARS Customs Bill of Entry, the underlying sale contract, and a reconciliation of all receipts; failure to repatriate within the statutory window is a criminal exchange-control offence. For export of services, such as sub-franchise advisory or supply-chain management fees invoiced to non-resident franchisees, payment must be received within 180 days of invoice or completion of the service, with the same repatriation obligation. For the inbound direction, payments to a foreign master licensor of franchise royalties or licence fees require a recognised exchange-control-approved licence agreement and full withholding-tax compliance before the outbound wire is approved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound subscription capital from the non-resident shareholder must be wired exclusively via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's own bank account to the South African entity's capital escrow or operational account at an Authorised Dealer. The swift message must use a defined BOP purpose category and state the underlying share-subscription agreement; the receiving bank will complete the inward BOP transfer record, and the company must submit its CIPC registration certificate, tax clearance letter, board resolution approving the allotment, and an updated share register. Genuine inward foreign direct investment requires no prior SARB approval, but if the remitter is not the named shareholder or funds arrive in fragmented third-party tranches, the Authorised Dealer will apply enhanced due diligence and may reject the transfer. Any single remittance above ZAR 10 million must be supported by a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN. If the cross-border financing is structured as a shareholder loan rather than equity, it must be declared as a foreign loan through the Authorised Dealer using the BOP loan category and a written term-loan agreement, with subsequent interest and principal remittances subject to interest withholding tax and exchange-control documentation. Recommended gold-standard routing: pre-notify the bank with the executed subscription agreement and source-of-wealth statement, use one declared shareholding wire per tranche, and maintain the capital account segregated from daily trading turnover until the share issue is finalised.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments use the SWIFT MT103 clearing rail for open-account supplier settlements and Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600) for larger procurement shipments of Malatang ingredients, soup-base seasoning, and packaging. All settlement in ZAR is cleared through SARB's Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system locally, while the cross-border leg is executed through the Authorised Dealer's correspondent banking network: USD via CHIPS/Fedwire, CNY via CIPS, and EUR/GBP via TARGET/CHAPS as applicable. For royalty and licence-fee disbursements to the foreign master licensor, the underlying master franchise agreement must be approved or recognised by FinSurv or processed through an Authorised Dealer under the applicable licensed-agreement framework, and every remittance must be supported by evidence that 15% domestic withholding tax on royalties was deducted and paid to SARS, reduced to any applicable treaty rate via a beneficial-ownership tax residence certificate where a double-taxation agreement applies. All outbound trade disbursements must reconcile to the supporting commercial invoice, customs Bill of Entry where goods are imported, packing list, bill of lading, and the import permit required for food additives or regulated agricultural inputs. Trade-finance instruments such as usance import L/Cs of 90 to 120 days and pre-shipment finance facilities may be layered onto the clearing rails to optimise working capital without contravening exchange-control rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (up to 12 months, renewable) against documented USD, CNY, or EUR exposures arising from firm import-purchase commitments and royalty remittance schedules.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permissible only where the underlying currency pair has no deliverable onshore market or the exposure is booked offshore; onshore rand NDFs are not recognised, and wielbare deliverable forwards remain the standard hedging mechanism.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS/CCS) to hedge long-term foreign-currency balance-sheet exposures, such as USD-denominated shareholder loans or offshore franchisee receivables, subject to Authorised Dealer approval and underlying documentation.
Vanilla FX Options (purchased only) to cap conversion costs on medium-term import and royalty outflows where the premium expense is commercially justified and no naked short positions are created.

FX Swaps and value-date swaps for efficient working-capital re-profiling within the same approved commercial exposure, available only with a full underlying trade or capital-flow rationale documented to the Authorised Dealer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation (company's annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue monthly; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years triggers CIPC administrative strike-off and deregistration; directors may be held personally liable for debts incurred during delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the CIPC Annual Return; any shareholding or beneficial ownership change must be filed within 7 business days after the change is recorded.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence; administrative fines up to ZAR 250,000 may be imposed; false or incomplete beneficial ownership information can result in criminal liability for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after financial year-end, or any later date stated in the official SARS provisional and final return notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% per month on assessed tax, capped at 100%; understatement penalties and possible criminal prosecution for persistent failure to submit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certificate of Acceptability (food premises) Annual Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Municipality Department of Public Health / Environmental Health Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before expiry of the current certificate; application generally submitted at least 30 days prior to the anniversary date of issue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid Certificate of Acceptability is an offence; municipal health authorities may close the premises, impose fines, and pursue prosecution under food safety legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the company's public interest score (PIS) is 100 or more; independent review by a registered accountant is required if PIS is between 50 and 99; compiled financial statements are permissible if PIS is below 50 unless the Memorandum of Incorporation or another regulator requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (International Financial Reporting Standards for Small and Medium-sized Entities) as endorsed in South Africa; full IFRS applies to publicly accountable entities; local GAAP is not applicable to (Pty) Ltd companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, coincident with the CIPC annual return filing, the company must confirm and file its beneficial ownership register. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be lodged with CIPC within 7 business days after the change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for companies with years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, s. 5(1)); prior-year rate was 28%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Corporation (s. 12E) graduated rates for qualifying (Pty) Ltd entities with gross income below ZAR 14 million: 7% up to ZAR 95,750; 21% up to ZAR 365,000; 27% above. General incentives: s. 12C manufacturing plant/machinery allowances (20% or 40% first-year); s. 12B renewable-energy assets (100% first-year allowance for solar PV and wind); s. 11D research-and-development super deductions; Employment Tax Incentive (ETI) for low-paid hospitality staff; full VAT input recovery on capital and operating costs where registrable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed year cap; assessed losses are carried forward indefinitely under s. 20(1) ITA, but only against taxable income derived from the same trade. Section 20A denies or restricts the set-off of losses where a shareholding change of more than 50% occurs and the company’s trade, or the financing of the trade, is not maintained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 — Corporate Income Tax Return for Companies; filed electronically through SARS eFiling under the company’s income-tax reference number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the year of assessment is the company’s financial year, generally the 12-month period ending on the last day of the month elected for accounting purposes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: SARS issues a filing-requirement notice; the ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after financial year-end. Provisional tax (IRP6) is paid during the year independently of the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, CIPC registration number, SARS income tax reference number, registered office and principal place of business, current contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders or directors must provide the foreign registered address and a South African agent authorised to receive SARS notices and correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Box 4 — Trade classification and year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary and secondary SIC codes; for the malatang self-serve fast-casual trade use SIC 6430 (Restaurants and Catering), corresponding to ISIC 5610.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entity must classify based on actual South African dining operations even where the franchise brand originates from China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from over-the-counter malatang sales, self-serve broth bowl charges, franchise licensing fees, rebates and any ancillary revenue; VAT collected must be excluded as it is not gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only gross income from a South African source is taxable under s. 9(2); foreign head-office charges or foreign-source receipts must not be included unless derived from a South African trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local dividends exempt under s. 10(1)(k) and domestic interest exemptions under s. 10(1)(i) where applicable; these reduce taxable income before deductions are applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends declared by the company to non-resident shareholders remain outside the company’s income tax but trigger dividend withholding tax on the shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 24 — Operating expenses and cost of sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Food ingredients and packaging, self-serve consumables, rent, payroll, utilities, repairs and maintenance, franchise royalty expense, bank charges, marketing and general administration costs actually incurred in producing income under s. 11(a).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may deduct only expenditure actually incurred in the production of South African-source income; allocations and notional head-office charges are disallowed under s. 23(m).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: s. 12C allowances on restaurant kitchen equipment and other plant used in production; s. 12B 100% first-year deduction for solar PV, battery, wind and biomass assets; s. 11D R&D allowances for recipe or supply-chain innovation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allowances are limited to the proportion of use that directly produces South African-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the assessed loss carried forward from the prior year; the loss is off-settable only against income from the same trade.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a non-resident carried on a South African trade, the assessed loss is available only while the same trade continues and s. 20A ownership/trade continuity tests are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 55 / Box 56 — Tax computation and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 27%, reduced by provisional tax (IRP6) credits, foreign tax credits under s. 6quat and any withholding tax credits; the net amount is the tax payable to SARS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must claim credits only for tax proved to be paid to SARS and for foreign tax attributable to South African-source income under the relevant DTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty per the SARS public-notice schedule, and for serious cases a fixed monthly penalty up to the statutory maximum for large companies; late payment attracts an automatic 10% lump-sum penalty under s. 195 TAA plus statutory interest under s. 187 at the repo rate plus 3.5% (approximately 11.75% per annum). Incorrect returns attract understatement penalties under s. 222–223 TAA ranging from 10% to 200% of the understated tax.
